pattern_explanation: These Portuguese words come from Latin roots shared with English, so they look familiar. Over time their meanings drifted apart, which makes them easy to misread.
false_friend_warning: Several Portuguese words look like English words but mean something different: the Portuguese word assistir means to watch or attend, pretender means to intend, and esquisito means strange or odd. Learners who translate by sight often choose the English word that looks similar, such as to assist for assistir or pretend for pretender.
